system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
These 3 questions belong together and follow one another in the test booklet.

## Question 1

A. Draw 1 straight line on this rectangle to divide it into 2 triangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

## Question 2

B. Draw 1 straight line on this rectangle to divide it into 2 rectangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

## Question 3

C. Draw 2 straight lines on this rectangle to divide it into 1 rectangle and 2 triangles.

[Image: Rectangle]

Figure, described in words:
An outline of an empty rectangle, wider than it is tall, with horizontal top and bottom sides and vertical left and right sides.

Answer each of the 3 questions.

output.answer_1: Draw one straight diagonal line from one corner of the rectangle to the opposite corner (for example, from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner). This cuts the rectangle into 2 triangles that are the same size and shape.
output.answer_2: Draw one straight line from the middle of the top side straight down to the middle of the bottom side, parallel to the left and right sides. This divides the rectangle into 2 smaller rectangles.
output.answer_3: Draw one straight line from the top side down to the bottom side, parallel to the left and right sides, to make a rectangle on one side. Then draw one diagonal line from a corner of the rectangle to the opposite corner, such as from the top-right corner down to the bottom-left corner, so that the rectangle on one side is cut into 2 triangles. The result is 1 rectangle and 2 triangles.
